question: What is the time shifting property of the Fourier transform?
_instructions: For each step set 'human_correct' to true/false. Set 'error_type' to one of: algebra, sign, missing_term, substitution, definition, none. Set '_filled' to true when done. Set 'final_answer_correct' to true/false after comparing 'generated_final' to 'expected_final'.

steps.description: Start with the definition of the Fourier transform of a signal x(t)
Consider the time-shifted signal x(t - t0)
steps.notes: Correctly sets up the FT of the shifted signal x(t - t0).

steps.description: Substitute variable: let u = t - t0, so t = u + t0 and dt = du
steps.notes: Correct substitution. Limits unchanged since shift is finite.

steps.description: Factor the exponential: exp(-I*omega*(u + t0)) = exp(-I*omega*u) * exp(-I*omega*t0)
Move the constant factor exp(-I*omega*t0) outside the integral
steps.notes: exp(-I*omega*t0) is constant w.r.t. u. Factoring out is valid.

steps.description: Recognize the remaining integral as the Fourier transform of x(u), which is X(I*omega)
steps.notes: Integral of x(u)*exp(-I*omega*u) du is X(omega) by definition. Correct.
